title: Inverse image of a constant sheaf
statement:
For a morphism of schemes $f:X\to Y$ and a $\Lambda$-module (or
complex of $\Lambda$-modules) $M$, the canonical morphism
$f^{-1}\underline{M}\to\underline{M}$ is an isomorphism on
$X_{\Et}$.

proof.text: Specialize the existing natural isomorphism AlgebraicGeometry.Scheme.upperStarConstantSheafIso of [lemma-constructible-pullback-constant] to ModuleCat Λ. Each component of its hom is invertible, so the module-sheaf clause follows by the standard IsIso instance. The existing isomorphism is constructed from uniqueness of left adjoints, and is precisely the comparison already fixed in the statement.

Apply CategoryTheory.NatIso.mapHomologicalComplex to that natural isomorphism and ComplexShape.up ℤ, using the termwise complex construction [def-kun-constant-sheaf]. Its hom is definitionally the NatTrans.mapHomologicalComplex appearing in the statement. Each component at a complex is therefore the hom of an isomorphism. The construction maps both the hom and inverse termwise and proves their inverse equations from the natural isomorphism equations; no boundedness assumption is involved.

proof_origin.place: P2: reuse the existing constant-sheaf natural isomorphism and Mathlib NatIso.mapHomologicalComplex; no stalk argument is needed
